name: QueueZero — Editorial Signal
intent: A confident hackathon product pitch that feels more like a sharp product launch/editorial technology story than a generic SaaS dashboard.
audience: hackathon judges and pilot decision makers
forbidden_aesthetics: neon cyberpunk decoration unrelated to the claim
full-slide device mockup on every product slide
four identical rounded cards as default proof layout

whitespace.rule: Whitespace is reserved around the visual protagonist before secondary content is placed; it is not leftover space after packing.

geometry.container_policy: use containers only when grouping is semantically meaningful

identity_anchors.description: A thin cobalt signal/path line with one emphasized node, used to visually connect sensing → prediction → decision or current → next state.
identity_anchors.semantic_requirement: must correspond to a real sequence, dependency, or destination

identity_anchors.description: Important numbers sit directly in open space at large scale rather than inside equal cards.
identity_anchors.semantic_requirement: must be the slide's strongest quantified conclusion

identity_anchors.description: A near-black field may occupy a bounded side or lower band to create a proof/ask destination and rhythmic contrast against the warm off-white canvas.
identity_anchors.semantic_requirement: must group proof, product, or terminal action rather than decorate

identity_anchors.description: A tiny slide-role/index marker may sit at one outer edge as a deck-navigation detail.

density_rules.low: One dominant idea, one support cluster maximum, large protected whitespace.
density_rules.medium: One protagonist plus two to five differentiated support objects; supporting objects may share a zone but should not become identical tiles by default.
density_rules.high: Remove decoration, merge semantically related support, and change composition before reducing title/hero hierarchy. If still overloaded, fail and request content reduction.

variation_rules: Alternate protagonist anchoring across adjacent slides when semantics permit.
Vary full-width, split-field, edge-anchored, and open-canvas compositions while preserving typography and identity anchors.
Use dark fields as rhythm punctuation, not as the default background.
Product screenshots may be staged, cropped, or detailed; do not repeat the same device-frame treatment on adjacent slides.
Metric evidence may be hero-number, scale, annotated comparison, or support cluster; do not normalize all metrics into cards.
anti_repetition_rules: Never use four equal metric cards on adjacent evidence slides.
Never repeat the same protagonist position on three consecutive slides unless the deck planner marks an intentional sequence.
Never repeat title + subtitle + centered four-box body as a generic fallback.
Do not use the signal_path anchor on every slide.
Do not place every visual inside a rounded rectangle.
Do not use more than one major dark field on adjacent slides.
Do not render every support fact with identical size and contrast.
